Usage:
## Subscribing

To use the websocket API, connect to
`wss://ws.backpack.exchange`.

To subscribe to a stream with the name `stream` send a text frame
over the websocket connection with the following JSON payload:

```json
{
  "method": "SUBSCRIBE",
  "params": ["stream"]
}
```

Similarly, to unsubscribe from a stream with the name `stream`:

```json
{
  "method": "UNSUBSCRIBE",
  "params": ["stream"]
}
```

You can subscribe or unsubscribe from multiple streams if you include
more than one in the params field.

All data from streams is wrapped in a JSON object of the following form:

```json
{
  "stream": "<stream>",
  "data": "<payload>"
}
```

The following command can be used to test subscribing to a stream:
```text
(sleep 1; \
echo '{"method":"SUBSCRIBE","params":["depth.SOL_USDC"]}';\
cat) |\
wscat -c wss://ws.backpack.exchange
```
The payloads for each stream time are outlined below.

## Timing

Unless documented otherwise, timestamps are in microseconds. K-line
start and end times use ISO 8601, and the stock-price `timestamp` is
the source timestamp in Unix milliseconds. The event timestamp is the
time the event was emitted from the websocket server, and the engine
timestamp is the time the event was generated by the matching engine.

If a message aggregates more than one event (for example, a depth
message), the engine timestamp will be the timestamp of the last
matching engine event.

## Keeping the connection alive

To keep the connection alive, a `Ping` frame will be sent from the
server every 60s, and a `Pong` is expected to be received from the
client. If a `Pong` is not received within 120s, a `Close` frame will be
sent and the connection will be closed.

If the server is shutting down, it stops accepting new connections
and, after a short delay, sends a `Close` frame to each client before
closing the connection. The client should reconnect after receiving
the `Close` frame. The client will be reconnected to a server that is
not shutting down.
Balance update:
Whenever the balance of an asset in the account changes, an update
will be pushed to the balance update stream with the new balance for
that asset.

Balance updates are not coalesced; a single settlement event can
cause multiple updates to be emitted, even for the same asset.

### Stream Name Format
- For all assets: `account.balanceUpdate`

The stream cannot be scoped to a single asset.

```json
{
  "e": "balanceUpdate",   // Event type
  "E": 1694687692980000,  // Event time in microseconds
  "a": "USDC",            // Asset
  "A": "122.35",          // Available quantity
  "L": "10",              // Locked quantity
  "S": "0",               // Staked quantity
  "T": 1694687692980000   // Engine timestamp in microseconds
}
```

The available, locked and staked quantities are the absolute balances
for the asset after the change, not deltas.
Position update:
On any mutation to a position the position will be pushed to the
position update stream. The event type of the position update will
be one of the following:

- `positionAdjusted`
- `positionOpened`
- `positionClosed`

On subscription, a message will be sent to the client with the current
open positions, if any. The `e` field will not be present in the
message.

### Stream Name Format
- For all markets: `account.positionUpdate`
- For single market: `account.positionUpdate.<symbol>`

```json
{
  "e": "positionOpened",  // Event type
  "E": 1694687692980000,  // Event time in microseconds
  "s": "SOL_USDC_PERP",    // Symbol
  "b": 123,               // Break event price
  "B": 122,               // Entry price
  "f": 0.5,               // Initial margin fraction
  "M": 122,               // Mark price
  "m": 0.01,              // Maintenance margin fraction
  "q": 5,                 // Net quantity
  "Q": 6,                 // Net exposure quantity
  "n": 732 ,              // Net exposure notional
  "i": "1111343026172067" // Position ID
  "l": "0",               // Deprecated placeholder, always 0
  "p": "-1",              // PnL realized
  "P": "0",               // PnL unrealized
  "T": 1694687692989999   // Engine timestamp in microseconds
}
```

The `l` field previously carried the estimated liquidation price. It
is a deprecated placeholder set to `0` and will be removed; clients
should not rely on its presence.

The net quantity field will be positive if the position is long and
negative if the position is short.

The net exposure quantity field includes exposure from the open
position, as well as any open orders.
Mark price:
Stream name format: `markPrice.<symbol>`

```json
{
  "e": "markPrice",           // Event type
  "E": 1694687965941000,      // Event time in microseconds
  "s": "SOL_USDC",            // Symbol
  "p": "18.70",               // Mark price
  "f": "1.70",                // Estimated funding rate. Not included for prediction markets
  "i": "19.70",               // Index price. Not included for prediction markets
  "n": 1694687965941,         // Next funding timestamp in milliseconds. Not included for prediction markets
  "T": 1694687965940999       // Engine timestamp in microseconds
}
```
